$comment: The incident register (IEC-CSO-EFR/DPR/EFI/IIR/OIR/FIR). Every incident is recorded here once, with its FedRAMP reportability evaluation and reason; a reportable one carries its Incident Rating estimates and the Initial, Ongoing and Final reports issued, each with when it was issued and what it set. scripts/_incidents.py validates it (fail-closed) and scripts/build-incident-report.py renders the reports and the incident log; .github/workflows/incident-reports.yml publishes them on every change to this file. The report clocks are FedRAMP's Class C timeframes, read from the pinned rules, never set here. Everything in this file is published. Exercises are marked exercise: true. Each resolved incident carries its lessons learned, each linking to the commit, decision or test that incorporated it (KSI-INR-AAR), and a pattern (root cause, component) that scripts/_incidents.py patterns() groups for recurrences (KSI-INR-RPI). Shape: infrastructure/schemas/incidents.schema.json.

policy.federal_incident_coordinator: Sam Aydlette, System Owner and incident response lead; contact through https://samaydlette.com/.well-known/security.txt
policy.notification_text: Published, and delivered to SIMULATED recipients. Each report is signed and published under https://samaydlette.com/.well-known/ (incident-reports.json lists every report and its sha256) and 'delivered' to a simulated FedRAMP and agency recipient, recorded in incident-deliveries.json. Nothing is sent to FedRAMP or to any agency: this system has no FedRAMP certification and no agency customers.
policy.federal_customer_data: None. This system holds no federal customer data (FRD-FCD) and has no agency customers. Were an agency to use the Silk Reeling application, what its users supply to it (pose landmarks) would be the federal customer data to consider; the operator's public site content, account information and the published evidence are not.

incidents.title: Exercise: internet-reachable likely exploitable N5 vulnerability in the Silk Reeling API
incidents.detection_source: Exercise inject: a simulated VDR finding that policies/triage.rego flags under VER-TFR-IRI

evaluation.reason: Simulated timeline. An internet-reachable, likely exploitable vulnerability rated N5 in a dependency of the Silk Reeling API. The operator treats such a vulnerability as a FedRAMP Reportable Incident (VER-TFR-IRI) until it is partially mitigated to N3 or below. The scenario assumes one agency whose users supply data to the application.
evaluation.federal_customer_data_considered: Scenario assumption: pose landmarks supplied by one agency's users of the Silk Reeling application. In reality the system holds no federal customer data.

estimates.reason: Exploitation could expose the landmark data of many of the assumed agency's users without interrupting the service for long; no other agency is assumed.

set.description: A request-parsing dependency of the Silk Reeling API has a vulnerability (simulated CVE-2099-0001) that an unauthenticated client could exploit over the internet to read other users' submitted data.
set.functional_impact: Potential loss of confidentiality of pose landmarks submitted by the assumed agency's users; no integrity or availability effect is expected.
set.recovery_plan: Throttle the affected endpoint now; upgrade the dependency to the fixed release and redeploy through the reviewed pipeline. Targets: partial mitigation within 3 hours, remediation within 1 day.

milestones.description: Triage flagged the finding under VER-TFR-IRI (simulated)

set.observed_activity: No exploitation attempts in the API Gateway access logs since the vulnerable release was deployed (simulated review).
set.root_cause: A vulnerable release of a request-parsing dependency (simulated CVE-2099-0001).
set.response_and_recovery_activities: Endpoint throttled at 04:15 (simulated), a partial mitigation; Incident Rating estimated at N3; fixed release identified.
Fixed release built and passing the pipeline's gates; deploy awaiting approval (simulated).
Fixed release deployed at 16:30 and the finding no longer appears in the VDR (simulated); recovery verified at 17:00.

pattern.root_cause: vulnerable release of a request-parsing dependency (simulated)

lessons_learned.lesson: An internet-reachable, likely exploitable vulnerability is an incident from its first evaluation, rated N5 until estimated, so its Initial report clock starts at once (AI-drafted).
A partial mitigation to N3 or below ends the incident treatment of the vulnerability; the pipeline recognises it without a person (AI-drafted).

incidents.title: Exercise: unauthorized change to a page of the public site
incidents.detection_source: Exercise inject: simulated drift of a website HTML artifact between the deploy-time and runtime KSI signals

evaluation.reason: Simulated timeline. The changed content is the operator's public site content, which is not federal customer data (FRD-FCD), and the change is not likely to affect the confidentiality or integrity of any federal customer data. Not a FedRAMP Reportable Incident; handled under the incident response runbook without FedRAMP reports.
evaluation.federal_customer_data_considered: None present: public website content only.

pattern.root_cause: unauthorized change to public site content (simulated)

lessons_learned.lesson: A page that changes between the deploy-time and runtime signals is drift, and drift is reported as a regression, never hidden by a read failure (AI-drafted).
Public site content is not federal customer data, so the change is evaluated not reportable and the reason is recorded (AI-drafted).
